title: Drought magnitude slopes were uncertain in three repeated bird study samples from a 2024 release
abstract: We tested whether greater drought magnitude predicted a more negative bird response within study, species, metric and shared-control groups. A 2024 public release supplied 51 paired rows in 17 blocks from three studies in Australia and Hawaii. Three-month slopes were -1.235, +0.282 and +1.286. Twelve-month slopes were -0.901, +0.229 and +0.120. All six corrected normal-reference intervals included zero when sampling correlations were unknown. Log response ratios kept all six slope signs. Omission checks showed unstable slopes. Overlapping periods and few weather histories prevent separate region and period replication. Field detection, endpoint labels, selected papers and unverified source extraction limit inference. This result does not show no drought effect. Code, source hashes, aggregate results, checks and a figure are included. External source records remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Within-group magnitude slopes in three study samples. Bars use maximum standard errors under unknown sampling correlations and six-test normal-reference correction. All intervals include zero. Scales refer to the released drought magnitude values.
